sections.heading: Iris, the Gorgons, and Pegasus
sections.translation:
Thaumas married Electra, daughter of deep-flowing Oceanus. She gave birth to swift Iris and the lovely-haired Harpies, Aello and Ocypete. On their fast wings they keep pace with gusts of wind and birds, darting high through the air.

Ceto bore Phorcys the fair-cheeked Graiae, gray-haired from birth. That is why the immortal gods and humans who walk the earth call them Graiae, the Old Women: Pemphredo in her beautiful robe and Enyo in her saffron-yellow robe.

Ceto also bore the Gorgons, who live beyond famous Oceanus, at the world's far edge toward Night, where the clear-voiced Hesperides live. They are Sthenno, Euryale, and Medusa, who suffered a terrible fate. Medusa was mortal; the other two could never die or grow old. Dark-haired Poseidon slept with Medusa in a soft meadow among spring flowers.

When Perseus cut off Medusa's head, great Chrysaor and the horse Pegasus sprang out. Pegasus got his name because he was born beside the springs of Oceanus; Chrysaor got his because he held a golden sword in his hands.

Pegasus took flight, leaving the earth, mother of flocks, and reached the immortal gods. He lives in Zeus's halls, carrying thunder and lightning for Zeus, the wise planner.
sections.summary: Electra gives birth to Iris and the Harpies. Ceto gives birth to the gray-haired Graiae and the Gorgons. When Perseus cuts off Medusa's head, Chrysaor and Pegasus spring out. Pegasus flies to the gods and carries Zeus's thunder and lightning.

cards.label: Thaumas
cards.general: A sea god.
cards.here: Electra's husband and father of Iris and the Harpies.

cards.label: Oceanus
cards.general: The divine river imagined as flowing around the world.
cards.here: Electra's father; the Gorgons live beyond his waters.

cards.label: Electra
cards.general: A divine daughter of Oceanus.
cards.here: Mother of Iris and the Harpies.

cards.label: Iris
cards.general: A goddess associated with the rainbow and a messenger for the gods.
cards.here: The swift daughter of Thaumas and Electra.

cards.label: Harpies
cards.general: Winged female beings whose name suggests snatching things away.
cards.here: Their wings carry them as fast as winds and birds.

cards.label: Aello
cards.general: A Harpy whose name suggests a storm wind.
cards.here: One of Electra's two Harpy daughters.

cards.label: Ocypete
cards.general: A Harpy whose name means “swift-flying.”
cards.here: Aello's sister.

cards.label: Ceto
cards.general: A sea goddess.
cards.here: Mother of the Graiae and the Gorgons.

cards.label: Phorcys
cards.general: A sea god.
cards.here: Father of Ceto's children.

cards.label: Graiae
cards.general: Their Greek name means “Old Women.”
cards.here: Hesiod explains their name through their gray hair, which they had from birth.

cards.label: Pemphredo
cards.general: One of the Graiae.
cards.here: She wears a beautiful robe.

cards.label: Enyo
cards.general: One of the Graiae; a different figure from the war goddess with the same name.
cards.here: She wears a saffron-yellow robe.

cards.label: Saffron-yellow
cards.general: A rich golden yellow, like the color made from saffron spice.
cards.here: The color of Enyo's robe.

cards.label: Gorgons
cards.general: Three fearsome sisters: Sthenno, Euryale, and Medusa.
cards.here: They live beyond Oceanus, near Night.

cards.label: Night
cards.general: Hesiod treats Night as a divine being.
cards.here: Her region marks the remote place where the Gorgons live.

cards.label: Hesperides
cards.general: Divine maidens associated with evening and the far west.
cards.here: Their clear voices are heard in the region where the Gorgons live.

cards.label: Sthenno
cards.general: One of the three Gorgons.
cards.here: She is immortal and never grows old.

cards.label: Euryale
cards.general: One of the three Gorgons.
cards.here: Like Sthenno, she is immortal and never grows old.

cards.label: Medusa
cards.general: The only mortal Gorgon.
cards.here: Perseus cuts off her head, and Chrysaor and Pegasus emerge.

cards.label: Poseidon
cards.general: The god of the sea, often called “the Dark-haired One.”
cards.here: He sleeps with Medusa in a meadow.

cards.label: Perseus
cards.general: A Greek hero.
cards.here: He kills Medusa by cutting off her head.

cards.label: Chrysaor
cards.general: His name means “Golden Sword.”
cards.here: He emerges from Medusa holding a golden sword, which explains his name.

cards.label: Pegasus
cards.general: A winged horse. Hesiod links his name with pēgai, the Greek word for “springs.”
cards.here: Born beside Oceanus's springs, he flies to the gods and carries Zeus's thunder and lightning.

cards.label: Zeus
cards.general: King of the gods, associated with thunder and lightning.
cards.here: Pegasus lives in his halls and carries his thunder and lightning.
